_about: Kinds of data for the Exposure Clock, each with the periods institutional sources document for how long that data stays protected: the x of Mosca's inequality. basis says which period the source sets: confidentiality (how long the information must stay secret), closure (how long access is barred) or retention (only how long a record is kept, at most a lower bound). defaults holds fixed periods, noEnd duties with no end in time. iso3 null is a general value for anywhere the Atlas holds nothing closer; euMembers carries an EU rule to each Member State without a period of its own. The post-quantum guides the Atlas quotes (the EU coordinated roadmap and its FAQ, the NCSC's Next steps white paper, ITSM.40.001, the ANSSI FAQ, the CISA, NSA and NIST factsheet, the NIST IR 8547 draft and the Dutch PQC Migration Handbook) were read on 4 October 2026: they name kinds of data with long confidentiality needs and thresholds such as at least 10 years, but set no period for any kind of data, so none is recorded here. A kind of data with no period for a place has none documented; the tool says so.
